title: You Are My Refuge and My Fortress

reflections.title: "You Are My Refuge"

reflect.text: God does not take us out of a dangerous world. Instead, He offers us a secret shelter within it, like a safe hiding place where tired people can rest. Trusting Him is like a high-rise worker leaning completely on a safety harness. We depend on His presence each day, knowing that God Himself is our fortress and safe retreat. Even when we cannot see it, His care surrounds us at all times, and His authority is greater than any peril.

Because this protection is real, we can thank the Lord in advance for keeping us safe. F. B. Meyer encourages us not merely to hold this truth in our heads, but to say it out loud: "You are my refuge." We need to keep speaking this truth because it is certain, not just when our feelings agree. Whether we are alone, facing opposition, or with friends, declaring our trust brings peace and helps us know His faithful character more deeply.

questions: Have you told the Lord out loud today that He is your safe refuge?
In what area of life do you need to lean on His unseen protection like a safety harness?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, You are our refuge and our safe fortress. Help us to depend on Your presence today and rest inside Your shelter. When we feel anxious or alone, give us the courage to speak our trust in You. Amen.

D10.author: Sarah Frazer
D10.work: Giving Thanks for the Hidden Refuge

reflections.title: "Under His Wings"

reflect.text: The Bible pictures God's care like a mother bird sheltering her young under her soft feathers. This picture shows both tender kindness and fierce defense. Real dangers surround us, including sudden fears in the dark, sickness, and spiritual arrows like bitter or evil thoughts. Scripture does not promise an easy life without hardship, but it assures us that God is right beside us in the middle of it. Knowing He is continually near gives us courage when our own strength runs out.

God is our sleepless guardian and faithful friend during the darkest hours. As Charles Spurgeon reminds us, darkness is not dark to Him, and He watches over us through every lonely moment. His truth acts like a solid shield and body armor that covers us from head to foot. Because the Lord cannot lie and never changes, His promises stand firm against every assault. We can lay aside our dread, nestle close under His wings, and find peaceful rest in His keeping.

questions: What nighttime worries or fearful thoughts do you need to bring under God's protective wings?
How does remembering God's faithfulness act like armor for your mind today?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You for watching over us without ever growing tired or sleeping. When dark thoughts and real dangers threaten our peace, remind us of Your faithful promises. Help us to nestle quietly under Your wings and trust Your gentle, mighty care. Amen.

reflections.title: Our Constant Home and Deliverer

reflect.text: Like the Israelites traveling through the wilderness, our lives on earth are filled with constant change. Our health, finances, and feelings may shift from one day to the next. Yet through it all, God remains our unchanging home. We are pilgrims passing through this world, but our true dwelling place is the Lord. Even if worldly hopes fade or joys wither, we lose nothing of what we have in God, because His love and relationship with us never change.

Along our path, the enemy sets hidden traps to pull us into sin and ruin. But God promises to rescue us from the hunter's snare. Sometimes He keeps us from stepping into danger by giving us spiritual strength to say no to evil. At other times, He uses painful trials to stop us before we destroy ourselves, turning us away from greater harm. Even if we stumble and get caught, the Lord does not throw us away. He calls the wanderer back, pardons our sins, and gently sets us free.

God also promises to set those who know His name safely on high. By His grace, God's kindness we do not deserve, we know Him as the One who hates sin yet pardons all our wrongs through Christ. We do not elevate ourselves by our own pride, which is always dangerous. Instead, God lifts us up into close fellowship and holy victory where the enemy cannot tear us down.

questions: How does knowing that God is your unchanging home bring comfort when your circumstances change?
Have you ever experienced God using a difficult season to turn you away from a worse trap?
reflections.prayer: Lord, You are our permanent home in a shifting and uncertain world. Thank You for forgiving our sins in Christ and rescuing us when we wander into danger. Keep our hearts close to You, and lift us into the safety of Your unchanging love. Amen.
